On October 17, 2026, the content dedicated to the week's Swiss current affairs presents a first SSR poll one year before the federal elections. The source does not suggest major political upheavals.
On October 16, another item describes a strengthening of polarization. The UDC leads the race and, with almost 30% of voting intentions, consolidates its position as Switzerland's largest party. The left is gaining ground, while the center-right parties are losing ground.
On the same day, the environmental dossier moves to Ticino. For the first time, the glaciers of Adula and Grauhorn are reported to be separated. The trip with experts from the canton serves to measure the effects of a changing climate. The report's title warns: «In a few years there will be no more glaciers in Ticino».
On October 14, the Solar Express project is presented as a promise that is still difficult to fulfill. The law was intended to accelerate the construction of alpine solar installations in Switzerland, but four years after its adoption, photovoltaics is still struggling to gain a foothold in the mountains.
### Institutional and international issues
Two items published on October 13 concern the functioning of the state and war materiel. The Swiss Parliament does not have the power to table a motion of no confidence against the Government. The source notes that this peculiarity, apparently undemocratic, also has some advantages.
On the same day, the Swiss population is called to the polls on November 29 to vote on a controversial proposal to amend the law on war materiel, aimed at easing its restrictions. On October 7, by contrast, the Swiss Government expressed its desire to establish a security partnership with the European Union, leaving open the question of whether the EU is willing to do the same. An item from October 6 also recalls that, while maintaining close ties with the EU, Switzerland does not intend to join it.
The review completes the picture with the issue of weapons available in homes: comprehensive data are lacking, and a motion calls on the Government to fill this gap. Finally, on October 2, the assessment of Swiss glaciers indicates that in 2026, summer heatwaves and scant winter snowfall led to the disappearance of dozens of glaciers. ## The practical reading of the dossiers
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the roundup should be read by separating the dossiers that are still open from the situations already described. This week's news do not amount to a single national decision: they bring together politics, institutions, security, relations with the EU, energy, and the environment.
The first point concerns the electoral calendar. The SSR poll captures voting intentions one year before the federal elections. The nearly 30% attributed to the SVP, the growth of the left, and the loss of support for center-right parties describe a shift in the balance of power indicated by the source, but do not constitute the election result. For the reader, the distinction prevents a political poll from being turned into a definitive prediction.
| Dossier | Distinction to maintain | |---|---| | Politics | Voting intentions and election result | | Weapons | Easing of the law and data on weapons in homes | | EU | Security partnership and membership in the European Union | | Environment | Alpine solar installations and glacier measurements |
The second point concerns institutions. The report on the no-confidence motion does not announce a new vote: it explains that Parliament cannot put forward that motion against the Government. The source also points to possible advantages of this approach. The issue therefore concerns the functioning of the Confederation and not a change already submitted to a popular vote.
The weapons dossier also requires precision. On November 29, the public will vote on easing the law on war materiel; separately, a motion asks the Government to address the lack of comprehensive data on weapons in homes. These are two different matters, and the source does not assign a decision date to the motion.
### Energy, ice and relations with Europe
At the European level, a security partnership and EU membership are not the same question: the Government wants the former, while Switzerland does not want to become a member of the EU. On the environmental front, the before-and-after comparison is explicit for Solar Express: the law aimed to accelerate alpine solar installations, but after four years photovoltaic power is still struggling to gain ground in the mountains. Measurements of Adula, Grauhorn, and the other glaciers add the cantonal and alpine dimension. The source does not quantify effects on wages, prices, or the cost of living; it is therefore not possible to derive precise amounts or economic consequences from these articles. ## A reading procedure for the week
To turn the roundup into a useful brief, it is advisable to proceed step by step and not merge together news items concerning different subjects.
1. Mark November 29 as the date of the Swiss population's vote on easing the law on war materiel. It is the clearest operational date indicated by the source.
2. Open two separate entries for the weapons issue. In the first, enter the vote on the law; in the second, note the motion calling on the Government to fill the lack of comprehensive data on weapons in homes. Do not assign the date of the vote on the law to the motion.
3. Record the SSR poll with the wording voting intentions and with the reference to one year before the federal elections. The UDC's nearly 30%, the left's growth, and the loss of support for center-right parties must be retained as elements of the poll, not as an already-decided election outcome.
4. For the European dossier, use two separate lines: security partnership and relationship with the European Union. The first concerns the Swiss Government's willingness; the second includes the question about the EU's willingness and the rejection of Swiss accession.
5. For the environment and energy, build a comparison between the objective and the observed situation. Solar Express aimed to accelerate alpine solar installations, while photovoltaics is still struggling in the mountains. For glaciers, note separately the measurement by the canton's experts and the assessment concerning the Swiss Alps.
The final check consists in not adding data that the source does not provide. The sentence about the glaciers in Ticino says «in a few years», not a precise date. The news about weapons in the home refers to an information gap, not a new count. The European dossier asks a question about the EU's willingness; it does not announce an agreement. This framework makes it possible to follow the Swiss political calendar without confusing a poll, a motion, a law, a measurement, and a partnership.

30'000 cubic metres of kerosene may be withdrawn from mandatory reserves. The country's Delegate for Economic Supply authorized its use on Thursday from October 15 to November 1. The quantity corresponds to 6,5% of what is available.
The intervention is linked to interruptions and considerable delays in international rail transport, especially from Germany. The reported risk is that Zurich Airport could run short of kerosene. The Confederation explains that trains are also failing to keep to schedule because large quantities of goods have been transferred to rail after river transport became impossible due to the low water level of the Rhine.
### What is guaranteed and what is under pressure The same communication specifies that Swiss supplies of petrol, diesel and heating oil have deteriorated compared with the previous week, but remain guaranteed. For people living in Switzerland, the wording therefore distinguishes between a deterioration in the situation and an interruption in availability: the note does not announce that these products have run out.
Asked about this, Zurich-Kloten Airport stated that, for now, departing aircraft are not subject to refuelling restrictions. UBAG manages the kerosene and deals with a total of nine external suppliers, including Socar, BP and Shell. All the fuel arrives at the airport by rail.
The airport management is not commenting on shortages at international level and refers to the airlines regarding refuelling flights bound for Frankfurt. Germany's main airport, which serves as a hub for Lufthansa, Swiss's parent company, is also experiencing difficulties. Lufthansa does not anticipate cancellations, but has invited crews bound for Frankfurt to depart with fuller tanks. ## The operational bottleneck is transport
The decision on reserves must be read together with one fact: all of the kerosene for Zurich-Kloten reaches the airport by rail. For this reason, disruptions to rail traffic directly affect the airport's fuel supply. The source links the difficulty to international delays, particularly from Germany, and to the diversion to rail of large quantities of goods that could no longer travel by river.

item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The UDC met on 17 October 2026 in Bulle. - No to the 13th AVS pension financed by an increase in VAT. - The people will vote on the items on 29 November. - Delegates say yes to spouses and war materiel.
## Key facts - Location → Bulle, canton of Fribourg - Delegates → approximately 420 - SVP president → Marcel Dettling - AHV recommendation → no, 290 votes to 3 - Official candidate → Céline Amaudruz - Voting date → November 29 - Vote on married couples → 274 in favor, 9 against, 3 abstentions - Vote on war materiel → 271 in favor, 16 against, 6 abstentions
On October 17, 2026, the SVP delegates' assembly held in Bulle, in the canton of Fribourg, focused on Swiss sovereignty, relations with the EU and the issues on the ballot. The party president, Schwyz National Councillor Marcel Dettling, attacked the left and those who, in his view, threaten self-determination and push for closer ties with the EU.
> We must stop the destruction of Switzerland.
Before approximately 420 delegates, Dettling linked the SVP's significant gains in the cantons since the 2023 federal elections to concerns about uncontrolled immigration, chaos in the asylum sector and the country's future. He then criticized the Bilateral III agreements with the EU and the parliamentarians who, in his view, would like to prevent a popular vote, also including Federal Councillors Cassis and Jans in his criticism.
Federal Councillor Albert Rösti was also present at the assembly. He argued for the need to defend a united Switzerland, direct democracy and institutions as factors of stability.
### The post-Parmelin period Discussion among the delegates also focused on what comes after Parmelin and on choosing the right person, man or woman, French-speaking or German-speaking Swiss. Céline Amaudruz is so far the only official candidate present in Bulle. SVP National Councillor Nicolas Kolly from the host canton was mentioned; he is still considering it, while a decision from Zurich's Natalie Rickli is also awaited. The final ticket must include at least one French-speaking Swiss, while the decision will be up to the Federal Assembly.
### Voting recommendations For November 29, the SVP recommended voting no on financing the 13th AHV pension through an increase in VAT: 290 votes to 3. Nicolas Kolly argued that the Confederation should make better use of the money entrusted to it by the Swiss and said that the Federal Council should have financed the 13th pension through savings in international cooperation and the asylum sector. Pierre-Yves Maillard said he would prefer higher taxation of high incomes and stressed that 80% of the 13th pension is financed by the AHV fund.
For the Centre Party's initiative on fair taxation for married couples, the recommendation was yes: 274 votes in favor, 9 against and 3 abstentions. The amendments to the federal law on war materiel received a yes vote, with 271 votes in favor, 16 against and 6 abstentions; Marc Jost spoke against them, invoking neutrality. Finally, the Central Committee had recommended voting no on the fireworks initiative. ## How to read the decisions of 29 November
The Bulle assembly produced political recommendations, not the outcome at the ballot box. For those living in Switzerland, the distinction is the first practical point: on 29 November, voters will vote on the items mentioned in the report, while the reported tallies describe the UDC delegates' vote. The party's position is not equivalent to the popular result: the text presents those numbers as the assembly's vote and 29 November as the date on which the people are called upon to vote.
### The debate over AVS funding The most concrete issue concerns the 13th AVS pension and its financing. The UDC is calling for a no vote on the increase in VAT and, through Nicolas Kolly, proposes seeking savings in international cooperation and the asylum sector. Pierre-Yves Maillard shifts the debate toward higher taxation of high incomes; at the same time, he points out that 80% of the pension is already financed by the AVS fund.
These are three points of reference that should be kept separate: the increase in VAT opposed by the UDC, the savings indicated by Kolly and the taxation of high incomes supported by Maillard. In the report, the first is the recommendation approved by the delegates; the other two are proposals put forward in the debate. For voters, the point to assess is therefore the financing method indicated in the question and the political debate over the resources to be allocated to the pension.
For the other items, the key to interpreting them is different. The Centre Party's initiative is presented through the principle of fair taxation for spouses and an end to discrimination based on marriage; the UDC's position is to vote yes. Regarding the Federal Act on War Materiel, the delegates approved the amendments, while Marc Jost invoked neutrality. On the fireworks initiative, the Central Committee opted for no the previous evening. The practical information provided by the report for these matters is the voting recommendation.
The European issue follows a separate track. The Bilateral Agreements III with the EU appear in Dettling's political attack; the passage on the recommendations of 29 November, by contrast, deals with AVS, spouses, war materiel and fireworks. This separation helps make sense of the day without conflating the debate over closer ties with the EU and the voting recommendations on the listed questions. The same logic applies to the post-Parmelin period: the discussion of the candidacies concerns the future political decision, while 29 November concerns the items put to the people. ## Preparing for the November 29 vote
Preparation can begin with the date indicated by the source: November 29. The practical step is to separate the questions and read the UDC's recommendation for each one, without turning the delegates' vote into the popular result.
### A five-step sequence 1. Set the date of the vote and identify the question on the 13th AHV pension. 2. For AHV, compare the question on the VAT increase with the alternatives mentioned in the debate: savings in international cooperation and asylum, or higher taxation of high incomes. 3. Examine the Centre Party initiative dedicated to fair taxation for spouses and ending marriage discrimination, with the UDC recommendation to vote yes. 4. For the amendments to the Federal Act on War Materiel, keep the delegates' yes vote distinct from Marc Jost's opposing intervention, based on an appeal to neutrality. 5. Consider the fireworks initiative separately, for which the Central Committee recommended voting no.
This outline avoids two confusions. The first is between the party's choice and that of the voters: the UDC has adopted voting guidelines, but the people are called upon to vote on November 29. The second is between the issues submitted to the polls and the political debate over Bilateral Agreements III with the EU. The report links the latter to defending self-determination and the possibility of a popular vote; in the section devoted to recommendations, however, it deals with the items already listed.
For those following the succession after Parmelin, the same rule means distinguishing between officially announced candidacies, names still under consideration, and the final institutional decision. Céline Amaudruz is the only official candidate present in Bulle; Nicolas Kolly is still thinking about it, Natalie Rickli still has to decide, and at least one French-speaking candidate will have to appear on the final ticket. The choice will then fall to the Federal Assembly. This dossier runs in parallel to the November 29 vote and should not be used to automatically interpret the individual ballots.

One video may show a werewolf’s bride transforming during intercourse; another tells the story of a woman’s pregnancy with a dragon prince. The scenes exploit the visual provocation that characterizes the format’s early days.
Behind this content are microdrama apps, platforms dedicated to short melodramatic series with sexual allusions. It is not just about the individual ad: behind the campaign is an entertainment model that moves from social media to a proprietary app.
### The format that brings viewers along
The episodes are shot vertically, last one or two minutes and end with a twist. The apps are free to download, and the initial episodes are also free; to continue, however, users have to subscribe and pay. Sexuality is often merely the initial hook. The plot weaves together three elements: the forbidden, represented by relationships with nonhuman beings, authoritarian leaders, enemies or dangerous creatures; metamorphosis, which may consist of an impossible pregnancy, a changing body or a hidden supernatural nature; and the twist, when the partner turns out to be a king, monster, billionaire or father of an heir destined to change the world.
Paolo Attivissimo, a technology journalist and popular science communicator, identifies young people and women as the most interested audience. In the United States, according to the cited data, the bulk of the audience consists of women aged 25 to 55; monthly users number 66 million, about one in six Americans, while CandyJar’s audience is said to be 99 percent female.
On the Swiss front, the institutional step cited by the source concerns the Federal Council, which on Wednesday passed the LPCom. Bern aims to strengthen protections for young people online, ensure transparency for Google and Facebook, and block targeted advertising, which exploits behavioral tracking and is used by microdramas. The message is expected by June 2027. ## The business beyond the provocative image
Comparing the costs helps explain why microdramas have become an industry. Attivissimo sets a traditional sitcom side by side with a production of 50–75 episodes:
| Production | Stated cost | |---|---| | Traditional sitcom | 2–4 million dollars | | 50–75-episode microdrama | 100–300 thousand dollars |
The source links the first figure to the sitcom’s production machinery: after success, actors ask for more money, while costume designers, catering, lighting technicians, sound engineers and set designers quickly drive up costs. The second format can be made with real actors or AI and condenses the story into very short vertical episodes.
### AI, production and work
The landscape, the source says, changed this year with Seedance 2.0, a model that generates videos much more realistic than previous ones. The model therefore makes the artificial generation used in ads and series more credible.
Attivissimo nevertheless draws a distinction: major film production remains superior; the technology will instead replace mediocre actors. Good actors and highly specialized specialists will continue to work, while those who perform generic work are at greater risk.
The business model is completed by the shift from social media to proprietary apps. Social media show the suggestive scene; the app avoids app-store commissions and monetizes each individual episode with micropayments. According to Attivissimo, sex remains implicit: it is not shown and can thus stay within the limits or evade checks. The expert adds that some social platforms are complicit when a channel brings in millions of dollars, despite official prohibitions.
### What it means for Switzerland
For the reader in Switzerland, the concrete consequence concerns targeted advertising. The source links microdramas to behavioral tracking and reports that the Federal Council aims to strengthen protections for young people online, ensure transparency for Google and Facebook, and stop that type of advertising. The dossier thus concerns how the ad reaches the user, not just the erotic content.
Attivissimo also envisions tailor-made stories, with a choice of emotion and eroticism, while systems insert the advertising. He cites Black Mirror as an already anticipated scenario and argues that AI, being unoriginal, will leave room for different niches, such as art-house films and vinyl records or CDs in music. ## The practical path to reconstruct
To correctly read an advertisement of this kind, it is useful to separate four stages: the trailer, the app, the payment and the federal dossier.
### 1. Recognizing the initial signal
The first step is social media: Instagram or TikTok. The clues are an AI-generated video, a scene somewhere between sex and fantasy, and a few words charged with narrative or emotional tension. The cases cited are the werewolf's bride and the dragon prince's pregnant woman. The content does not necessarily tell the whole story: sexuality may be merely the initial hook, while the series develops themes of the forbidden, transformation and a twist.
### 2. Following the transition to the app
The second moment is the redirection. The advertisement takes the user away from social media, toward the proprietary app of the microdrama. The platforms cited are ReelShort, DramaBox and ShortMax. Initial access is free, and the first episodes also do not require payment. The progression is built around one- or two-minute vertical episodes, each ending with a twist.
### 3. Separating free access and spending
The third step is the financial one. To continue the series, one must subscribe and pay; the model also includes micropayments for each episode. Attivissimo indicates a cost of about 20 francs to watch an entire series, but points out that it can reach 200 dollars per month. The source associates the first amount with watching the entire series and the second with monthly subscriptions. This distinction helps avoid confusing free access to the app with free viewing of the entire catalog.
### 4. Keeping the federal deadline separate
The final step concerns the Swiss dossier, not the individual episode. The Federal Council approved the LPCom on Wednesday; the message is expected by June 2027. The stated objectives include greater protection for young people online, more transparency for Google and Facebook, and a ban on targeted advertising based on behavioral tracking. For the reader, this distinction avoids confusing how the apps work with the announced institutional phase.
The final check follows a precise sequence: advertisement on social media, transfer to the app, initial free episodes, a request for a subscription or micropayment and, in the public sphere, awaiting the federal message by the stated deadline. It is this chain, more than the individual fantasy scene, that explains how the microdrama turns attention into revenue and how the issue of targeted advertising entered the federal dossier.

On October 17, 2026, in Hanoi, President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin was received by President Tô Lâm and Prime Minister Lê Minh Hưng. The official visit focused on bilateral relations between the two countries. In this context, agreements were concluded in various political areas. The signing of the free trade agreement bringing together the four EFTA members and Vietnam is also scheduled for Sunday, October 18.
### A relationship placed on a new footing
Switzerland and Vietnam have maintained diplomatic relations for 55 years. In 2026, the establishment of a global partnership gave relations between the two countries a new direction. Since 2008, Vietnam has been one of Switzerland's priority countries for economic cooperation. The programme for the 2025-2028 period supports sustainable trade and innovation, promotes financial-sector stability and advances industrial and urban development compatible with climate protection.
Both sides highlighted the opportunities associated with the free trade agreement. The signing is also described as a political signal in favour of open, rules-based trade. The talks touched on the interest in concluding negotiations for a modernized agreement on investment protection, with the aim of strengthening legal certainty for investments.
The international situation and the two countries' cooperation as members of the UN Human Rights Council were also on the table. The delegations also discussed negotiations on cooperation against climate change, pursuant to Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
During the visit, Switzerland and Vietnam signed several bilateral conventions, including the launch of two development-oriented economic cooperation projects. These initiatives are geared towards implementing the free trade agreement and sustainable urban development; they also aim to improve the framework conditions for trade and investment and strengthen long-term competitiveness. Some declarations of intent concern the labour market, employment and innovation. Following the meetings with Tô Lâm and Lê Minh Hưng, talks with Trần Thanh Mẫn and other government representatives are planned. The Swiss-Vietnamese economic forum and the signing of the agreement are also scheduled for October 18; Parmelin is accompanied by a delegation from the business community. No already visible effects for businesses or workers are quantified.
The same applies to investment protection. Switzerland and Vietnam have expressed interest in completing negotiations for a modernized agreement. Legal certainty is identified as an objective, not as a result already achieved. The news therefore does not present the negotiations as a new operational framework.

This distinction avoids turning a diplomatic objective into an immediate effect on the Swiss economy. To follow the dossier operationally, without attributing effects to it that the source does not announce, it is advisable to use a monitoring sequence.
### The operational sequence
1. Set the calendar. October 17, 2026 identifies the official visit and talks in Hanoi. October 18 is the date indicated for the signing of the free trade agreement and for the Swiss-Vietnamese economic forum.
2. Classify the status of the acts. The bilateral conventions and economic cooperation projects appear to have been signed during the visit. The free trade agreement, on the other hand, is announced for the following day. The negotiations on investment protection and climate cooperation are still described as ongoing.
3. Read the objectives without adding details. In subsequent documents, it is necessary to verify the actual content relating to trade, investment, innovation, sustainable urban development and competitiveness. The source indicates these objectives, but does not provide further implementation conditions, amounts or deadlines.
4. Separate the project from the result. The two projects aim to improve framework conditions and support sustainable urban development. To assess their concrete effect, it is necessary to await the elements describing implementation, without presenting the objective as an already achieved result.
5. Isolate the employment dimension. The statements of intent on the labor market, employment and innovation should be considered a commitment to strengthen cooperation. They are not presented as announcements of new positions or as new procedures for workers.
For the general public, the source does not indicate forms, requirements or individual deadlines. The most appropriate course of action is therefore to distinguish what has been signed, what is scheduled and what remains under negotiation. The economic delegation and the forum provide the point of observation for following the commercial dimension; the texts of the agreements will instead serve to verify the actual content.

item.description: The SP launches an initiative on gender-based violence in Thun The delegates unanimously approve the project At least 500 million additional francs
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The SP launches an initiative on gender-based violence in Thun - Delegates approve the project unanimously - At least 500 million additional francs requested each year - Signature collection planned to begin in spring 2027
## Key facts - Initiator → Swiss Socialist Party - Location → Thun - Resources requested → at least 500 million additional francs per year - Approval → unanimity among the delegates - Next step → legal review by the Federal Chancellery - Signature collection → spring 2027
On Saturday, during the congress of the Swiss Socialist Party in Thun, the delegates unanimously approved launching a popular initiative to strengthen the protection of women from violence and combat gender-based violence. The project is not limited to calling for more prevention: it also proposes closer cooperation between the Confederation, the cantons and specialized services.
The financial demand is explicit. The PS is calling for at least 500 million additional francs to be made available each year to combat gender-based violence. The party argues that support for victims still depends too much on their place of residence and considers the progress made in this area insufficient.
To support its position, the PS recalls that 27 femicides were recorded in Switzerland in 2025 and that there have already been 18 cases since the beginning of this year. Tamara Funiciello, National Councillor and co-president of Socialist Women, described femicides as merely the tip of the iceberg, also citing rapes, beatings, humiliations and discrimination. “Protection costs money, but violence costs lives,” she said.
### The institutional step
Federal Councillor Beat Jans also spoke at the congress. He argued that domestic and gender-based violence are not private matters, but a responsibility of the state governed by the rule of law and society as a whole.
Thun’s green light does not conclude the process: before the PS launches the signature collection, scheduled for spring 2027, the text will have to undergo legal review by the Federal Chancellery. In her speech, Socialist co-president Mattea Meyer accused the UDC of having “a structural problem with violence,” citing visits to Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping and tributes to Donald Trump. ## The territorial issue
The proposal's most concrete implication concerns the relationship between place of residence, services and institutional levels. The SP starts from the observation that support for victims still depends too much on their place of residence. Viewed from a national perspective, this criticism shifts the focus: it is not enough to demand a response to violence; it is necessary to ask to what extent prevention and assistance are coordinated among the Confederation, Cantons and specialized services.
### More resources, but with what structure
The request for at least 500 million additional francs each year introduces a precise financial dimension, but the available text does not define how the resources should be distributed. The source does not specify amounts for individual Cantons, allocation criteria, programs to which the funds should be allocated or a control mechanism. For this reason, it is not possible to translate the figure into a concrete benefit for an individual or an expense attributable to a territory. The key issue to watch in the debate will be the link between funding and objectives: strengthened prevention, institutional cooperation and a response less dependent on place of residence.
For anyone living or working in Switzerland, the distinction between a proposal and a measure currently in force is decisive. The available text does not describe a new service, a change to support arrangements or the immediate disbursement of 500 million. The source places the project in a preliminary phase: the text still has to undergo legal review by the Federal Chancellery, and signature collection is scheduled to begin only in spring 2027. Until that stage, the operational fact is therefore political and procedural, not a change that has already been implemented.
Beat Jans's intervention is also indicative. Defining domestic violence and gender-based violence as a responsibility of the rule-of-law state and society as a whole broadens the scope of the discussion, but does not indicate new responsibilities or concrete obligations. Mattea Meyer's position on the SVP belongs to a different level: it is a political criticism of the party and its leadership, not a decision on the initiative. Separating these levels helps avoid confusing the requested funding, the organization of services and the debate between parties. ## How to follow the process
For the reader, the most practical approach is to follow the indicated stages and not anticipate the effects of a proposal still in progress. The sequence available is short, but each step has a distinct meaning.
1. Recognize the current phase. The project was unanimously approved by the PS delegates meeting in Thun. This signals the congress's decision, not the entry into force of a new protection or new funding.
2. Await the legal review. The text will have to be submitted to the Federal Chancellery. This is the next stage indicated by the source; the collection of signatures is planned for spring 2027.
3. Mark spring 2027 on the calendar. The PS plans to begin collecting signatures then. For the public, the practical reference is therefore the season announced by the party.
4. Assess the content through four questions. Does the proposal aim to strengthen prevention? How does it address cooperation among the Confederation, Cantons and specialized services? How does it link this cooperation to the request for at least 500 million additional francs every year? Does it respond to the criticism that support depends too heavily on place of residence? These are the criteria that emerge from the project and the PS's rationale.
### Separate facts, positions and accusations
When following the dossier, it is advisable to distinguish the congress decision from the political statements. Funiciello explained the need to invest in protection; Jans described combating violence as a task of the rule of law and society; Meyer criticized the UDC and referred to a case involving a former Aargau cantonal parliamentarian accused of abuse. These are statements present in the news coverage, but they do not amount to an outcome of the initiative or a judicial decision on the case cited.
In the phase described by the source, the actionable point is to keep the timeline and content distinct: the PS's approval, the subsequent legal review and the planned collection of signatures are known; no new services, cantonal amounts or individual procedures are described. This distinction prevents a political request from being turned into an already operational measure.

item.title: UDC rejects VAT hike to fund 13th AVS pension; vote Nov 29
item.description: UDC says no to the VAT increase for the 13th AVS pension payment The people vote on the proposal on November 29 In Bulle, no wins by 290 votes to 3
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - UDC says no to the VAT increase for the 13th AVS pension - The people vote on the proposal on November 29 - In Bulle, the no vote passes by 290 votes to 3 - The Udc says yes to Centro's initiative
## Key facts - Subject → financing the 13th AVS pension through VAT - UDC decision → no, with 290 votes against 3 - Vote → November 29 - Location → Bulle assembly (Fr) - AVS fund → finances 80% of the 13th pension - UDC alternative → savings in international cooperation and asylum - Maillard alternative → higher taxation of high incomes - Centre initiative → yes, with 274 in favor, 9 against and 3 abstentions
With 290 votes against 3, UDC delegates recommended voting no on financing the 13th AVS pension through an increase in value-added tax. The decision was taken at the party assembly held Saturday in Bulle (Fr), while voters will go to the polls on November 29.
The issue under discussion is not the mere existence of the 13th pension, but its funding mechanism. The proposal put to the vote in fact provides for an adjustment to VAT. UDC chose to reject it and turned the no into an official recommendation to voters.
During the assembly, Fribourg National Councillor Nicolas Kolly argued that the Confederation should make better use of the money entrusted to it by the Swiss. In his view, approval of the principle of a 13th AVS pension did not amount to consent to a new tax increase. For this reason, UDC would have preferred the Federal Council to finance the benefit through savings, citing funds earmarked for international cooperation and the asylum sector.
Pierre-Yves Maillard, a Vaud Socialist and Council of States member as well as president of the Swiss Trade Union Federation, would have opted for higher taxation of high incomes. However, he stressed the need to identify an additional source of funding, given that the AVS fund already covers 80% of the 13th pension.
### Two recommendations on the same date
The result in Bulle therefore yields two distinct recommendations: no to financing the 13th AVS pension through VAT, yes to the Centre initiative. The two recommendations should not be confused: the first item concerns the pension's funding source, the second fiscal fairness between spouses. ### Three questions for assessing the proposal
To interpret the vote from the perspective of someone living in Switzerland, it is useful to keep three aspects separate. The first is the benefit: the 13th AVS/AHV pension. The second is the financing: the VAT increase provided for by the proposal. The third is the political choice of the source of the funds: VAT, the savings indicated by the Udc, or higher taxation of high incomes. This distinction prevents the vote on financing from becoming an undifferentiated judgment on the AVS.
The text brings the decision to the national level. VAT is a federal lever; it is not the same as direct federal tax and is not a change decided autonomously by the Cantons. When assessing the cost of living, the point to isolate is therefore the tax channel chosen to support the 13th pension. The news makes it possible to compare the mechanisms without turning the debate into a personal calculation.
| Option | What the source indicates | Related position | | Avs increase | Financing the 13th Avs pension | Proposal put to the vote | | Savings | International cooperation and asylum sector | Udc preference, as reported by Kolly | | High incomes | Higher taxation to find resources | Maillard's preference | | Avs fund | Coverage of 80% of the pension | Data cited by Maillard |
This comparison also clarifies the role of the Federal Council in the Udc's reasoning: according to Kolly, it should seek the necessary savings instead of supporting a new tax increase. Maillard's position starts from a different premise: an additional source remains necessary, even though 80% of the 13th pension is already financed by the Avs fund.
For a resident, the choice therefore does not boil down to the question of whether the 13th pension is desirable. It is necessary to assess which of the indicated sources should be placed at the center. The reference to VAT makes the issue federal; the reference instead to taxation of high incomes and savings shifts the comparison to the distribution of the financial burden. These are the three elements to keep together before casting the vote. ### Four steps before November 29
1. Pin down the first issue: the vote concerns financing the 13th AHV pension through VAT, not a general question about social security.
2. Separate the benefit from its financing. You can consider separately the principle of the 13th pension and the method proposed to finance it.
3. Compare the alternatives mentioned in the debate: the SVP's opposition to a VAT increase, the savings in international cooperation and asylum cited by Nicolas Kolly, or higher taxation of high incomes, preferred by Pierre-Yves Maillard.
4. Keep the second initiative separate. The Centre proposes the text on fair taxation for spouses and the SVP recommends voting yes; this position does not coincide with the no vote expressed on financing the 13th AHV pension.
The first step is meant to prevent reading the SVP's no as an undifferentiated rejection of the pension. The position approved in Bulle concerns financing it through VAT. The second helps to understand the point raised by Kolly: for the SVP, approving the principle of the 13th pension did not entail accepting a new tax increase.
In the third step, noting the different sources avoids confusing a savings proposal with a proposal for higher taxation. The figure indicating that 80% is financed by the AHV fund should be read together with Maillard's request to identify an additional source nonetheless.
Finally, anyone assessing both issues must treat them as two separate choices, also because the SVP's recommendation changes from one issue to the other. To connect the pension debate to your own situation, consult guida AVS/LPP and calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: AI lends its voice to scammers: how to defend yourself against suspicious calls
item.description: An Italian bank is alleged to have lost 95 million euros.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - An Italian bank is said to have lost 95 million euros. - A company in the canton of Schwyz lost several million francs. - The UFCS report concerns the first half of 2026. - The verification must be carried out through another channel.
## Key facts - Italian case → 95 million euros - Swiss case → company in the canton of Schwyz; several million francs - Report → UFCS; first half of 2026 - Calls from fake officials → 75% drop - Online identity theft in Switzerland → 2%, 80%, 3%
A fraud based on altering a voice using artificial intelligence reportedly caused an Italian private bank to lose 95 million euros. In Switzerland, by contrast, a company in the canton of Schwyz lost several million francs following phone calls that reproduced the voice of a business partner.
The increasingly widespread use of generative AI tools will make this type of fraud more common. The risk concerns both individuals and companies, especially when a familiar voice is used to make a financial or IT request seem credible.
### A familiar voice is not proof
On the RTS programme On en parle on October 8, 2026, Sandy Lavorel, founder of FlairSafe, identified verification through a second channel as the main defence:
> It is advisable to contact the person again using another channel to confirm their identity, especially if a payment is requested or if you are asked to communicate a code or provide a password.
Lavorel also recalls a basic rule of digital hygiene: slow down. Scammers exploit urgency to push victims to act without thinking. Even when the voice sounds like that of someone very familiar, it is important to avoid making decisions under pressure and to verify the request through a different channel.
FlairSafe is a free platform that helps identify online scams. It currently does not specifically detect voice-cloning fraud, but it can analyse the risk level of a message via a screenshot or copied-and-pasted text. Discussions are under way with several partners to develop this feature.
The latest report by the Federal Office for Cybersecurity, covering the first half of 2026, notes that the use of AI in scams continues to increase. Attackers use it to create personalised and credible content. Targets include company employees, while CEO fraud uses an artificial voice that imitates that of a superior to persuade employees to make illicit bank transfers.
The related material on Switzerland also reports a 75% drop in calls from fake officials, following new rules that block spoofed foreign numbers. The material on online identity theft in Switzerland also includes the percentages 2%, 80% and 3%: these are data referring to that related material and are not attributed to the two voice-cloning cases described here. ## Why verification must move beyond the phone call
The threat described by the source changes how a request must be assessed. The problem is not merely listening to a modified voice, but deciding whether a voice alone can confirm the identity of the person speaking. The answer indicated by the source is no, even when the caller seems familiar.
### Familiarity and authenticity are two different things
A phone call may sound as though it is coming from a business partner, a superior, or someone familiar. This element makes the request more credible, but does not replace checking through another channel. The decisive step is to separate what is said on the phone from identity verification: the phone call brings the request, the callback is used to check it.
Urgency is the other element to treat with caution. According to Sandy Lavorel, scammers often pressure the victim to act without thinking. For this reason, slowing down is not simply a pause, but the way to prevent pressure from determining the decision. When the request concerns a payment, a code or a password, the need to change channels becomes particularly clear.
For companies, the procedure has a concrete consequence for daily work. An employee may receive a phone call supposedly from a business partner or a superior. In CEO fraud, the artificial voice is used precisely to persuade employees to make illicit bank transfers. Verification should therefore not stop at recognizing the voice or the role claimed by the caller.
The before-and-after comparison is stark. Before verification, the request remains a communication received under pressure. After moving to another channel and calling the person back, the caller must confirm their identity and the request. The source does not present the tone of voice as a sufficient tool for carrying out this check.
FlairSafe, too, must be placed correctly in the sequence. The platform can analyze screenshots and copied-and-pasted texts, but it does not yet specifically detect voice cloning. If the main element is a phone call, the protection described by the source remains slowing down followed by verification. The case of the company in the canton of Schwyz shows why the rule also applies to people working in Switzerland and not only to private individuals exposed to online messages. ## What to do when a suspicious phone call comes in
The procedure indicated by the source can be applied without trying to technically recognize the voice. The objective is to prevent the pressure of the call from immediately turning into a payment, the disclosure of a code or the handing over of a password.
### Operational sequence
1. **Slow down.** Do not make a decision while the caller insists on the urgency. The pause helps escape the pressure scammers use to push people to act without thinking.
2. Identify the request. Clarify whether the call is asking for a payment, a code or a password. These are the situations for which the source recommends verifying the identity through another channel.
3. Change channels. Stop automatically trusting the voice and call the person back to verify their identity. The check must take place outside the received call.
4. Apply the same rule to familiar voices. The fact that the caller seems to be a business partner, a superior or someone you know does not eliminate the need to call back and verify.
5. Analyze any related messages. If the request is accompanied by a message, you can submit it to FlairSafe via screenshot or by copying and pasting the text. The platform assesses the message's risk level, but does not yet specifically detect voice cloning.
### The sequence for those who work in a company
An employee who receives a request attributed to a business partner or a superior can apply the same steps before proceeding. The source indicates that company employees are often targeted to steal large sums; for this reason, verification should not be set aside when the voice sounds authentic.
Switching to another channel is also the point that distinguishes message analysis from identity confirmation. FlairSafe can help assess a text or a screenshot, while a phone call with a cloned voice requires the callback indicated by Lavorel. Ongoing discussions with several partners specifically concern the development of a feature for this type of fraud.
The operational rule therefore remains straightforward: slow down, identify what is being requested, change channels and verify the person. This is the procedure to apply even when the voice really seems to be that of someone you know well.

item.title: Same income, different taxes: savings of up to 90%
item.description: For the same income, the municipality changes the tax bill.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - With the same income, the municipality changes the tax bill. - One case reaches over 90% in savings. - The most advantageous municipality depends on income and family.
## Key facts - Source → Tages-Anzeiger analysis based on data from the Federal Tax Administration - Comparison → 20 types of households and 27 income brackets - Case → family with two children and 150mila gross francs - Les Verrières → 13,57% in taxes - Baar → 1,34% in taxes - Difference → 18'351 francs per year - High income → approximately 164'500 francs in Freienbach and Wollerau - Vaud comparison → 363'500 francs in Château-d'Oex and several Vaud municipalities
Considering a family with two children and a total gross income of 150mila francs, in Baar, in the Canton of Zug, taxes amount to 1,34%, compared with 13,57% in Les Verrières, in the Canton of Neuchâtel. The difference reaches 18'351 francs per year and, in the case examined, the saving exceeds 90%.
An analysis by the Zurich daily Tages-Anzeiger, based on data from the Federal Tax Administration, compared the tax burden of Swiss municipalities for 20 different types of households and 27 income brackets. The data show that there is no single tax haven: the most advantageous municipality varies according to income and family composition.
### A ranking that changes
For a household with two children and an income of one million francs, approximately 164'500 francs in taxes are paid in Freienbach and Wollerau; in Château-d'Oex and several other Vaud municipalities, the amount rises to 363'500. The difference approaches 200mila francs.
The Canton of Zug remains favorable also for the middle class: a family with two children and two salaries pays no income tax on total earnings up to 100mila francs.
The picture varies from one canton to another. Geneva is relatively affordable for the lower-middle income bracket, but proves more costly for high incomes. Appenzell Innerrhoden, on the other hand, is more favorable to affluent taxpayers, while in Bern the tax burden remains high for almost all income categories.
The comparison covers municipal, cantonal and federal income taxes. Wealth taxes, church taxes and other fees are excluded; moreover, the effective tax burden may vary depending on individual deductions. For this reason, the ranking describes comparable tax profiles, not an identical answer for every taxpayer.
The key point remains residence: with the same income, the municipality can significantly change the bill. But as soon as income or family structure changes, the location at the top of the comparison changes too. ## Tax savings are not the total cost
### Rent can change the outcome
Tax data, considered on its own, is not enough to decide where to live. The same analysis warns that rents can erase the advantage gained on the tax bill, especially for households with low incomes. In municipalities that are more tax-efficient, rents in fact tend to be high; localities with a higher tax burden may prove less expensive overall when housing costs are lower.
The practical comparison must therefore combine two perspectives, without turning the tax ranking into an absolute ranking:
| Profile | Signal from the source | Practical interpretation | | --- | --- | --- | | Lower income | housing can weigh more than taxes | compare rent with tax savings | | Higher income | the map of advantageous municipalities changes | use the correct bracket and family | | Different families | affordability depends on composition | do not apply one result to every household | | Different personal data | deductions can change the effective burden | read the comparison without considering it definitive |
This logic avoids taking the result referring to a family with two children and applying it to any household. The analysis considered 20 types and the result shows that the number of children, family composition, and income shift the outcome. A municipality that appears highly competitive in one bracket may not be so in another.
The word taxes must also be read precisely. The comparison includes income taxes at the municipal, cantonal, and federal levels, but not wealth, church, and other taxes. A difference shown in the ranking therefore does not cover every item that may affect a family's finances. Individual deductions can also change the effective burden.
For those considering moving to a different municipality, the question is not only how much the tax bill decreases, but whether the new housing cost really results in savings. For low incomes, the second figure may weigh more than the first; for high incomes, the tax comparison may be broader, but it remains tied to the family profile and the bracket considered. Affordability should be understood as a balance between these items, not as a permanent label for the municipality. ## From comparison to personal verification
To use the comparison correctly, it is advisable to turn the data into a structured verification. The process does not start with the Municipality that appears at the top, but with the household profile and the income to be compared.
### Five steps for a consistent verification
1. Set the reference income. Use the total gross income indicated for the family and place the case in the relevant bracket. The analysis is based on 27 brackets, so a result should not automatically be moved from one bracket to another. 2. Define the family. Indicate the number of children and the composition of the household; if there are two salaries, the data must be retained in the profile, because the map changes with the family structure. 3. Compare Municipalities and do not stop at the Canton. The source’s results are municipal, and the most favorable locality changes depending on the profile examined. 4. Consider housing costs alongside taxation. Put the rent of the locality being considered next to the tax difference. For a low-income household, this item may weigh more than taxes and may cancel out the savings. 5. Check the scope. Verify that the calculation covers municipal, cantonal and federal income taxes, and remember that wealth taxes, church taxes, other fees and individual deductions remain separate factors.
The final result should be read in two stages. First, identify the Municipality that is most tax-favorable for your profile; then check whether housing costs change the overall balance. If the income or family composition changes, the comparison must be repeated: the source shows that the most advantageous locality is not fixed.
The same method prevents confusing a comparison between taxes with a promise of automatic savings. The Municipality’s data must be considered together with the family, the income bracket and the items excluded from the analysis. Personal verification must therefore keep the tax calculation and the housing calculation separate, so as not to attribute to the former savings that the latter may reduce.
For a first personal estimate, use calcolatore stipendio/imposte.

item.title: Swiss healthcare system: LAMal 2026 guide for the Canton of Geneva
item.description: Mandatory insurance, deductibles and premiums: how LAMal works in Geneva in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - LAMal insurance requirement: within 3 months of arrival - Adult deductibles: CHF 300/500/1000/1500/2000/2500 - Premiums: broken down by canton and region - Subsidy: cantonal premium reduction
## Key facts - Obligation → residents - Deadline → within 3 months of arrival - Adult deductibles → CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 - Premium → per capita; it is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution - Variability → canton/region - Premium reduction → cantonal subsidy
Within three months of arrival, anyone residing in Switzerland must take out the compulsory health insurance provided for by LAMal/KVG. This is the operational deadline from which to begin the 2026 guide to the Swiss healthcare system, including for those living in the canton of Geneva. LAMal is private insurance with per-capita premiums: it is not a tax and it is not a payroll contribution.
### One common rule, cantonal variables The rule requiring insurance is national. Premiums, however, are structured by canton and region, while premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. For Geneva, this means that the comparison must be based on the premium applicable to the area and on the support provided by the Canton, not on a figure presented as identical throughout Switzerland. The guide cannot indicate a specific amount for Geneva without verified data.
The choice of insurer and deductible are the two practical steps placed at the center of the guide. For adults, the deductibles listed are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500. The list serves as a framework of options; on its own, it cannot promise precise savings or reimbursement. Without the premium applicable to the canton or region, it is not possible to attribute automatic value to the chosen deductible or replace missing data with unverified figures.
### LAMal is not a payroll deduction The premium must be kept separate from contributions linked to salary. AVS/AHV, AI, IPG, AD/AC, LAINF/LAA and LPP/BVG belong to the payroll contribution system; LAMal instead follows the logic of the per-capita premium. Direct federal tax and VAT are also different items: AFC/ESTV is responsible for these two taxes, while cantonal administrations oversee the cantonal and municipal levels. UFAS/BSV concerns social security and UST/BFS statistics. Distinguishing these levels prevents healthcare spending from being treated as a rate on salary.
For those living in Geneva, the starting point therefore remains threefold: comply with the three-month deadline, choose the deductible from among the adult options, and verify the area-specific premium and cantonal subsidy. Comparison with the rest of Switzerland serves to separate the common rule from the cantonal variables. ## Geneva in the national comparison To read the canton of Geneva correctly, one must separate what remains the same from what changes. The LAMal requirement and the three-month deadline do not become a different rule simply because the premium is linked to the canton or region. The territorial variable affects the comparison of premiums and the subsidy; it does not turn insurance into a cantonal tax.
| Item | National framework | Reading for Geneva | |---|---|---| | Obligation | Residents; enrollment within 3 months of arrival | Check the personal deadline | | Adult deductible | CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, 2500 | Compare the option chosen | | Premium | Per capita; canton/region | Use the territorial reference | | Reduction | Cantonal subsidy | Check the cantonal rule |
### The cost to budget In the family budget, the premium must be calculated as an item separate from salary. It is not correct to look for a percentage to apply to the payslip, as one would for a payroll contribution. The difference affects how the cost of living is measured: the comparison should place the per-capita premium alongside the chosen deductible, without confusing the amount with AVS/AHV, LPP/BVG or other employment deductions.
A hypothetical case shows the limits of quick comparisons. A resident may be faced with the six adult deductibles; the list alone cannot establish which choice is more advantageous, because the framework contains neither a concrete premium nor a reimbursement calculation. The choice must therefore be considered together with the health insurance fund and the territory, rather than by isolating the deductible amount.
The same caution applies to averages. Average LAMal premiums appear among the figures indexed each year. For a 2026 guide, using an unverified amount risks turning the national comparison into an outdated or inappropriate figure for Geneva. It is better to use the documented mechanism: premium by canton or region, cantonal subsidy and selected adult option.
The Cantons, moreover, are not a mere graphic detail of the table. The source assigns them a role in premium reduction, just as it assigns cantonal and municipal taxation to cantonal administrations. For healthcare, this leads to a practical consequence: the national component guides the choice, while verifying support requires the competent cantonal level. ## How to proceed in 2026 The procedure can be organized without using unverified figures. The objective is to turn the rules of LAMal into a personal checklist, keeping obligation, choice, premium, and subsidy separate.
### Five operational steps 1. Set the arrival date. The deadline runs from arrival, and the policy must be taken out within three months. This is the first check for every resident, including in the canton of Geneva. 2. Identify the insurance choice. Compare insurers and select an adult deductible of CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000, or 2500. Do not replace the list with a deductible not provided by the source. 3. Read the premium within the correct scope. The premium is per capita and refers to a canton or region. For Geneva, the relevant territorial data must therefore be used; a national average cannot automatically be treated as a personal figure. 4. Verify the cantonal reduction. The subsidy is cantonal: verification must be carried out according to the rules of the competent canton, without confusing it with direct federal tax, VAT, or AVS/AHV and LPP/BVG contributions. 5. Complete the comparison with a consistency check. The LAMal premium is not a deduction from salary. If the estimate mixes per-capita premiums and salary contributions, separate the items before assessing the cost of living or the sustainability of the choice.
### What to leave out of the calculation Invented amounts are not needed to complete the procedure. Average LAMal premiums and other figures in the Swiss system may be indexed every year; for 2026, it is advisable to use only verified data relating to the canton or region. The same criterion applies to the subsidy: without a requirement, deadline, or amount present in the source, fields should not be filled in with assumptions.
The practical elements to check are therefore limited: arrival date, chosen insurer, adult deductible, territorial premium, and verification of the cantonal subsidy. The guide does not authorize inferring other amounts or treating the premium as a tax item. Anyone comparing Geneva with the rest of Switzerland obtains a comprehensible result only by maintaining this distinction.
For the final operational step, confronta LAMal e cassa malati.

item.title: AI helps Swiss shoppers but stalls at checkout
item.description: Almost 70% of Swiss people use AI for a purchase 49% say that AI influences their choice 67% want to keep payment autonomous Only 17% accept
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Almost 70% of Swiss people use AI for a purchase - 49% say that AI influences the choice - 67% want to retain autonomous payment - Only 17% accept a fully AI-driven purchase
## Key facts - Source → Visa study - Survey → online survey published Thursday - Sample → more than 1'200 people in Switzerland - Age range → 18-65 years - AI use → nearly 70% to prepare a purchase - Influence on choice → 49% of users - Autonomous payments → 67% of respondents - Fully autonomous purchase → 17% of respondents
Nearly 70% of Swiss people have already used AI-based assistants to prepare a purchase. This is shown by an online survey published Thursday, conducted on behalf of Visa among more than 1'200 people living in Switzerland, aged 18 to 65.
For nearly one in two (49%) of those who use these tools, AI strongly influences the purchase decision. Among the same users, one in ten has already bought the very product recommended by AI. For some respondents, therefore, the assistant guides the consumer all the way to the specific choice of item.
The link between recommendation and the exact purchase makes the reported influence visible: for some users, the suggestion does not remain merely an abstract comparison. The threshold changes, however, when the choice has to become a payment.
### The trust threshold is reached at checkout
Trust decreases at the payment stage: 67% of respondents prefer to handle it themselves in every case. Only 17%, by contrast, would accept a fully autonomous purchase, including payment.
One third of respondents, equivalent to 33%, would accept giving the AI agent some freedom in completing the purchase, provided that the amount was set in advance and generally remained limited. 24% would allow autonomous purchases, including payment, up to 50 francs; above 100 francs, the share would fall to 2,5%.
The figures distinguish two stages of shopping. In the first, the assistant can help search and choose; in the second, the user wants to retain control over the expenditure. The willingness to delegate does not disappear, but remains tied to a financial threshold set in advance.
The study thus captures a behavior already present among Swiss consumers, without describing a generalized shift to automated payments. Visa commissioned the survey; the results measure respondents' preferences, not a change in payment rules. The most concrete data point for reading the survey concerns the type of purchase. AI assistance is expected above all for complex purchases: bookings for travel and transport reach 33%, while purchases of electronics and technology products reach 28%. For weekly shopping, the share is 20%. The distribution indicates that the assistant is more often associated with a choice involving several options than with a recurring purchase.
| Area | Share indicated in the study | |---|---:| | Bookings for travel and transport | 33% | | Electronics and technology products | 28% | | Weekly shopping | 20% | | Risk of losing control over spending | 55% | | Misuse of payment data | 51% |
### The problem is not only the recommendation
The 55% of respondents are primarily concerned about losing control over spending, while 51% identify misuse of payment data as a risk. Taken together, these figures explain why trust may be higher in the research phase and lower when the assistant approaches authorization of the spending. The practical question is not only whether the suggested product is appealing, but also how much leeway to give the agent and which data are included in the payment process.
For a Swiss consumer, this distinction makes it possible to separate comparison from delegation. An assistant can be used to organize information about a trip, transport, an electronic device or a technology product; the act of spending, however, remains the point at which reservations become most visible. Weekly shopping, at 20%, appears less associated with assistance than the complex categories identified by the survey.
The study highlights a generational divide: Generation Z turns to AI more than previous generations. Comparing suppliers using AI is approved by 82% of young respondents, compared with 71% of older people. This greater openness does not, however, eliminate the demand for security and control: Generation Z demands the same level in both respects. The figure suggests that familiarity with the tool and willingness to delegate payment are not equivalent. Anyone who wants to use an AI assistant for shopping can organize the process so as to keep decision-making support and payment authorization separate. The survey results make it possible to turn this distinction into a practical sequence, without assigning AI the same role in every purchase.
### Before confirmation
1. Define the task. Determine whether the assistant should help decide what to buy, where to buy it, or compare suppliers. The initial request should remain focused on research and guidance, not automatically become an order.
2. Set the scope. Indicate which purchase you are preparing for and what amount you are willing to consider. A preset limit makes clear the threshold within which potential autonomy is evaluated.
3. Separate advice and order. Treat the recommended product as a proposal to verify before making the final choice. AI’s influence on the decision does not amount to accepting a fully autonomous purchase.
4. Decide who pays. If the goal is to retain control, keep the payment step manual. If partial delegation is being considered, authorization must remain tied to the limit established beforehand.
5. Check two risks. Before confirmation, ask whether the transaction could lead to losing control over spending and whether payment data could be misused. These are the two main reservations that emerged from the survey.
This sequence makes it possible to use AI as an assistant, without automatically turning a recommendation into a transaction. The function can stop at comparison, preparation, or suggestion; the decision to pay remains a separate step. The user can thus choose a level of assistance consistent with the preset amount and their own need for security.
The method keeps the boundary between convenience and delegation clear: first define what to ask, then delimit autonomy, and finally confirm the payment. To connect purchase management with everyday expenses, consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
*Source: [rsi.ch](https://www.rsi.ch/info/svizzera/L%E2%80%99IA-aiuta-i-consumatori-svizzeri-a-fare-shopping--4164661.html)*

item.title: Discount retailer freezes 2027 hikes, staff discount doubles
item.description: Denner does not plan general increases in 2027 The employee discount rises from 10% to 20% Pension fund contributions increase by 1,2 points Minimum
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Denner does not plan general increases in 2027 - The employee discount increases from 10% to 20% - Pension fund contributions increase by 1,2 points - The 2026 minimum wages continue to be paid thirteen times
## Key facts - Company → Denner, discount retailer of the Migros Group - Decision → no general wage increase in 2027 - Discount → from 10% to 20% starting next year - Minimum wages → introduced at the beginning of 2026 - Payment → thirteen times a year - Pensions → employer contributions +1,2 percentage points - Employee share → unchanged - Benefits → new rotating monthly promotions
BERN — Denner has decided to forgo general wage increases for 2027. The discount retailer belonging to the Migros Group is instead focusing on strengthening benefits for its staff.
Starting next year, the employee discount will rise from 10% to 20%. The measure was announced the day after Migros had decided to award its employees ten times the Cumulus points on purchases, providing an equivalent benefit to a 10% discount. The two companies are therefore pursuing different strategies: Migros intends to invest further in wages, while Denner is not planning a general increase.
### Unchanged wages and minimum already set
The company justifies the decision by pointing to the particularly difficult market environment. The minimum wages introduced at the beginning of 2026 will be maintained and will continue to be paid thirteen times a year; according to Denner, the minimum wages guaranteed to employees will remain above the industry average.
The comparison provided by the company concerns 2026: Denner's minimum wages were higher than those of Migros and Coop, but slightly lower than those of Aldi and Lidl. The source does not report the amounts, but indicates the discount retailer's relative position compared with the competitors mentioned.
### Pensions and new promotions
Denner will strengthen pension benefits to compensate for foregoing the increases. Thomas Kaderli, the company's spokesperson, explained that, in the second pillar, the employer contributions paid into the pension fund will increase by 1,2 percentage points. The employee share will remain unchanged.
The doubling of the discount and the strengthening of occupational pension benefits will be supplemented by rotating monthly promotions, in addition to the benefits already in place. The choice announced for 2027 therefore shifts support for employees from general pay to a combination of benefits and pension provisions. To read the announcement from the perspective of someone who works at Denner, it is useful to separate three elements: pay, benefits and pension provision. They do not have the same effect on daily life and cannot be added together as though they were a single salary component.
### Comparing the different components
| Item | Available information | Announced effect | |---|---|---| | Salaries | Minimums introduced in 2026 and paid 13 times | No general increase in 2027 | | Employee discount | Current 10% | 20% from next year | | Pension fund | Second pillar | Employer +1,2 points; employee share unchanged | | Promotions | Existing benefits | New rotating monthly offers |
The discount provides a benefit linked to its use. For those who use it, the increase from 10% to 20% makes the same perk more advantageous; the actual benefit, however, depends on the purchases made and does not automatically amount to a pay increase. The decision therefore does not offer a single figure applicable to every employee.
Pension provision follows a different logic. The increase borne by the company concerns the pension fund and the second pillar, i.e. occupational pension provision under LPP/BVG. The employee's share remains unchanged: the announcement therefore describes a strengthening of the pension component without indicating an increase in the personal deduction.
The reference to minimum wages should also be read separately. Denner maintains that in 2026 its own thresholds were higher than those of Migros and Coop and slightly lower than those of Aldi and Lidl. For those assessing the labor market or the cost of living, this comparison helps distinguish the level of pay from additional perks, but does not make it possible to calculate an advantage in francs.
The announced package may therefore be more interesting in different ways: the discount affects the immediate benefit, while the pension fund concerns retirement provision. The source does not provide information to determine which of the two components weighs more for each individual employee. A collaborator can monitor the implementation of the measures through an orderly review, distinguishing what concerns pay from what concerns benefits and pensions.
### A checklist for 2027
1. Retain the current reference point. The starting point is the current 10% personal discount, together with the minimum wages introduced at the beginning of 2026 and paid thirteen times a year.
2. Check the new benefit. In 2027, Denner's communications should be checked for the application of the 20% discount and the rotating monthly promotions. The two measures should be recorded separately: one is the personal discount, while the others are additional offers.
3. Separate the pension item. In salary or pension documents, the figure to monitor is the 1,2 percentage-point increase in contributions paid by the employer to the pension fund. According to the announcement, the employee's share must remain unchanged.
4. Do not turn percentages into unavailable figures. The source does not state the amounts of the minimum wages or the monetary basis on which to calculate the company contribution. It is therefore advisable to record the percentage changes without deriving an unspecified value in francs.
5. Assess an offer as a whole. To compare Denner with Migros, Coop, Aldi or Lidl, four columns can be kept separate: minimum wage, payment in thirteen instalments, personal discount and pensions. The comparison of minimum wages remains the one declared by Denner for 2026.
This approach avoids two opposite errors: considering the doubling of the discount as a pay increase or ignoring the strengthening of pensions because it does not appear in immediate compensation. For an orderly review of remuneration items, consult guida alla busta paga svizzera.
